line: Walt is late again. Do you play? Chess, xiangqi, either. I'm not fussy.
A little is enough. My father taught me on a board drawn on cardboard. Red moves first. Sit.
You again. Good. Walt only plays one opening. It's very boring to beat him.
I built bridges for thirty years. Chess is the same. Everyone looks at the pieces. I look at what holds them up.
My wife says don't speak Chinese loudly in the park now. I said we've been in this park since 1994. She says speak quietly anyway.
The radio says the new president will clear the citizenship backlog. My sister has waited eleven years. I'll believe it when she calls me.
You come to the center on Thursdays now? Good. Old Wu needs a partner. He cheats, but slowly.
You and Walt are friends now. He told me you're improving. He lies, but it was nice of him.

choice1: Sorry I brushed you off before.

line: Mr. Lin has the paper folded to the xiangqi problem. "Red to move, mate in three. Everyone here says it's impossible. You play?"
Lin. My father taught me on a board drawn on cardboard. Look, the chariot here, the horse there. In the park I play Walt's chess. Here I get the real one.
You again. Old Wu is late and his tea is getting cold, so I'm drinking it. Don't tell him.
My wife says don't speak Chinese loudly in the park now. We've played in that park since 1994. So in here, I speak loudly. Old Wu complains.
